questions.def: 'Bread' is uncountable, so we use 'some'.
questions.question: We need to buy ___ bread for the party.

questions.def: 'Sugar' is uncountable, so use 'much' for negatives.
questions.question: There isn't ___ sugar in my coffee.

questions.def: 'Advice' is uncountable; use the noun form.
questions.question: I need some ___ on this matter.

questions.def: 'Information' is uncountable, so we use 'some'.
questions.question: She gave me ___ useful information.

questions.def: 'Experience' is uncountable; use 'a lot of'.
questions.question: He has ___ experience in marketing.

questions.def: 'Furniture' is uncountable, so use the singular.
questions.question: They bought new ___ for their house.

questions.def: 'Water' is uncountable, so use 'some' for requests.
questions.question: Could you give me ___ water, please?

questions.def: 'Time' (duration) is uncountable, so use 'much'.
questions.question: How ___ time do we have left?

questions.def: 'Work' (tasks) is uncountable here; use singular.
questions.question: He has a lot of ___ to do.

questions.def: 'Paper' is uncountable, so we use 'some'.
questions.question: I need ___ paper to write on.

questions.def: 'Apples' is countable, so use 'many'.
questions.question: There are ___ apples on the table.

questions.def: 'News' is uncountable, though looks plural.
questions.question: I have some good ___ for you.

questions.def: 'Money' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negatives.
questions.question: I don't have ___ money on me.

questions.def: 'Students' is countable, so use 'many'.
questions.question: How ___ students are in the class?

questions.def: 'Knowledge' is uncountable; use the noun form.
questions.question: He has a vast ___ of history.

questions.def: 'Tea' is uncountable, so we use 'some'.
questions.question: She drank ___ tea this morning.

questions.def: 'Friends' is countable, so use 'many'.
questions.question: He has ___ friends in this city.

questions.def: 'Luggage' is uncountable; use the singular.
questions.question: We had too much ___ to carry.

questions.def: 'Traffic' is uncountable, so use 'much'.
questions.question: There is ___ traffic on the road today.

questions.def: 'Advice' is uncountable, use 'some'.
questions.question: He gave me ___ useful advice.

questions.def: 'Electricity' is uncountable; use the noun form.
questions.question: The house has no ___.

questions.def: 'Information' is uncountable; use 'some'.
questions.question: I need ___ information about the course.

questions.def: 'Chairs' is countable; use 'many' in negative sentences.
questions.question: There aren't ___ chairs in this room.

questions.def: "Sugar" is uncountable; "some" is used for affirmatives.
questions.question: We need to buy ___ sugar for the cake.

questions.def: "Time" is uncountable; "much" is used for uncountable nouns.
questions.question: I don't have ___ time to waste on that.

questions.def: "Information" is uncountable; use the noun form.
questions.question: I need ___ about the flight.

questions.def: "People" is countable; "many" is used for countable nouns.
questions.question: There are ___ people waiting outside the building.

questions.def: "Water" is uncountable; "some" is used in requests.
questions.question: Could you give me ___ water, please?

questions.def: When generally referring to skill, "experience" is uncountable.
questions.question: He has ___ in marketing.

questions.def: "Furniture" is uncountable; "some" is used for affirmatives.
questions.question: They have ___ furniture in their new house.
